audit.why: 51.6% over 2308 games with Darius owning levels 1-5, an even 6 and both item stages matches full.phases and the already-audited kassadin__darius mirror exactly (inverse ratings 6/4, 7/3, 7/3, 7/3, 5/5, 6/4, 6/4). No chart change needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike called Riftwalk 'short-range and expensive' with no number, and phases[4].why never said why the pull still beats the blink.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 500 range on a 5/3.5/2s cooldown; Apprehend is 535 range on 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s. The pull out-reaches the blink at every rank, and the escalating mana cost on chained casts is the real punish, not the cooldown.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, whys[4], mid and phases[4].why now carry the 535-vs-500 range fact and Riftwalk's 5s.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[5].t was the generic 'Track Kassadin's Riftwalk' stub and named no actual interaction. Nether Blade's auto reset appeared nowhere.
audit.why: Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic damage only; Decimate and Hemorrhage are physical and Noxian Guillotine is true damage, so the shield reads zero against Darius - the kassadin__darius mirror reached the same conclusion from the other side. Force Pulse charges off spells cast nearby and Darius only casts three, so it is rarely charged in this lane. Nether Blade is an auto-attack reset, so his wind-up is the tell, not the cast.
audit.corrected: report[5].t rewritten around the shield and Force Pulse charging; spikes[0].text now names Nether Blade as the reset.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns was three generic clauses with no durations at all.
audit.why: Apprehend 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s is the longest cooldown in the lane and is the entire engage; Decimate is 9/8/7/6/5s; Noxian Guillotine is 120/100/80s, costs no mana at rank 3 and refreshes on a kill.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with real numbers; dosFull[2].d now states Riftwalk's 5s.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. Track it before every engage. - Your engage/committal tool: never waste it on chip damage. - Your ultimate: the win condition — spend it on kill windows, not on waves.
edits.after: - Apprehend: 26s at rank 1 and still 16s at rank 5 — it is the whole engage, so a whiff hands him the wave. - Riftwalk: 5s at rank 1 and 2s at rank 3; his escape is a timer, so drain the mana, not your patience. - Noxian Guillotine: free at rank 3, refreshed by a kill.

edits.before: Track Kassadin's Riftwalk: His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. When it is down — Pull + Q him down.
edits.after: Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic only and you deal physical and true. Force Pulse barely charges — you cast three spells.

edits.before: Noxian Guillotine turns any 5-stack trade into a kill. The execute resets on takedowns — all-in windows are now real kill windows.
edits.after: Noxian Guillotine at 5 stacks kills and refreshes on a takedown, but Riftwalk is 5s — land the 535-range pull first or he blinks off.

edits.before: Kassadin wastes Riftwalk — commit the full combo immediately.
edits.after: Kassadin wastes Riftwalk — commit now, it is back in 5s.

edits.before: Kassadin is miserable pre-6 — his Q shield only blunts magic and he has no waveclear speed, so E Apprehend into Decimate-Crippling bullies him off farm and you should be denying levels.
edits.after: Kassadin is miserable pre-6 — Null Sphere's shield blunts magic only, so it reads zero on you, and Apprehend into Decimate-Crippling Strike bullies him off farm. Nether Blade is his auto reset.

edits.before: His R Riftwalk gives an escape, but the first cast is short-range and expensive; you still win the all-in if you E on top of him before he can chain blinks away.
edits.after: Riftwalk reaches 500 on a 5s cooldown and every chained blink costs more mana; Apprehend reaches 535, so pull first and he cannot leave before the execute lands.

edits.before: Level 6 your all-in still beats his short, costly first Riftwalk.
edits.after: Level 6: your 535 Apprehend out-reaches his 500-range Riftwalk.

edits.before: From 3 through the first item you stay ahead: even after 6 his short first Riftwalk can't reliably escape a well-timed Apprehend, and your job is to convert every lane win into a lead that ends the game early.
edits.after: From 3 through the first item you stay ahead: Apprehend reaches 535 and Riftwalk only 500, so the pull lands before he blinks, and your job is converting every lane win into a lead that ends it early.

edits.before: Use Riftwalk to dodge your E and R commitment
edits.after: Riftwalk out of Apprehend before the pull lands
